headline: Rain arrives tonight into Saturday, then cooler, mostly dry weather into next week.
summary: Warm, dry weather ends as a front approaches from the west, pushed along by a dip in the jet stream (a trough) as a high-pressure ridge moves east. Most rain falls late tonight into early Saturday, mainly along the coast and in the mountains. Afterward, a convergence zone, where winds meet and air rises, may keep showers going near the Snohomish and King county line. Saturday highs cool to the upper 50s and lower 60s. Sunday is cooler and mostly dry. Next week looks drier: a low offshore Monday should barely clip the area, with at most a shower or two on the coast, and Tuesday brings light, dry easterly winds. A weak front may bring light rain Wednesday into Thursday.
changes: The morning discussion expected showers on the coast Monday, while the afternoon and evening discussions called Monday mostly dry with at most a shower or two on the coast. The evening discussion also added a Small Craft Advisory for waves on the outer coastal waters Saturday.
